content:
jamie: quick flag — bringing up praxis7b-sparse (hf->onnx->runtime) and after int4 quant we see a big summarization quality drop vs fp16 baseline. not a perf regression, quality only. anyone seen this pattern?

rachel: how big is big? numbers please :eyes:

bench-bot: summary run (eval-suite v2) — fp16 rouge2=0.121, int4 rouge2=0.051; fp16 ROUGE-L=0.382, int4 ROUGE-L=0.295; ppl on longform test 1.8 -> 2.9 (relative). latency same +/- 5%.

sudeep: two common culprits: rotary parameterization mismatch or tokenizer id offsets during conversion. conversion log?

jamie: conversion command we used: ```python convert.py --from hf --model praxis7b-sparse --out onnx/praxis7b-int4 --quant int4 --rotary_scale 1.0 --token-map preserved``` logs looked normal.

noel: runtime expects rotary_scale ~0.875 by default for this family (we did that historically for sparse-head models). if conversion forced 1.0 you can get phase misalignment -> weird attention patterns. also check per-head sign flips if using headwise permute.

anya: i ran a quick ablation: re-export with --rotary_mode per_head_scale and rotary_scale=0.875 then run the same eval snippet. rouge2 went 0.051 -> 0.093 (partial recovery). still not fp16 but better. i can push the artifacts to s3:/redwood-temp/praxis7b/rotary-checks/ if helpful.

jamie: that's encouraging. any idea why tokenizer would cause this though? we used the HF tokenizer that comes with the model from the hub.

sudeep: HF tokenizer can be identical but conversion steps sometimes produce a token-id remap when merging vendor merges/bpe vocab transforms. if token ids shift, kv-cache and rotary alignment with tokens can be off. quick check: run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(tokenizer.encode('The quick brown'))"` on both the original and converted artifacts and diff ids.

noel: also watch sentinel/placeholder tokens — praxis7b-sparse had two extra BOS aliases in its tokenizer.json which we hadn't accounted for; that produces a +2 offset in some converter codepaths we patched earlier for other families.

jamie: i ran the encode diff like you said and there is a consistent +2 offset for tokens >= 50256. weird boundary.

anya: i tried a simple remap (apply offset -2 to ids >= 50256) at runtime during tokenization and re-ran 50 samples. rouge2 recovered to 0.108 and many hallucination cases reduced. it's a hack but confirms token-id offset is a major factor.

bench-bot: quick micro-bench after remap test: rouge2=0.108, ROUGE-L=0.365, ppl=1.95. throughput unchanged.

sudeep: ok, so two factors: rotary scale mismatch + token-id offset. combined they can amplify distributional shift after quantization. quant noise interacts badly with phase misalignment.

jamie: plan: 1) pin tokenizer artifact from HF (sha256: abc123...) and add assert in converter to detect id offset boundaries, 2) re-run convert with per_head_scale=0.875 and preserve-token-ids flag, 3) run standard eval-suite v2 and report. i'll open an onboarding issue.

noel: +1. also add a small unit test in our convert CI that checks `encode(text)` id equality between hf and converted tokenizers for a 100 sample bank. avoids silent shifts.

anya: i'll upload the temporary artifacts and a short notebook showing the remap experiment: s3:/redwood-temp/praxis7b/rotary-tokenid-repro.ipynb. put it in the PR for visibility.

jamie: thanks all — workaround is validated. i'll file PR 1234 with converter patch, CI test, and a note in the onboard checklist about "rotary_scale family defaults" and "token-id aliasing". tagging @sudeep for review. :rocket:
